item.title: The right of way in Dublin
item.content:encoded:
Nature Cities, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00540-x

At the front gate of Trinity College Dublin, trams, buses, taxis, bicycles and pedestrians compete for the same seconds of green. Xiaowen Tao reflects on how a city decides, signal by signal, who goes first and whose time is worth more, and argues that those decisions deserve to be debated as openly as any other public choice.
item.dc:title: The right of way in Dublin
item.dc:creator: Xiaowen Tao

item.title: Institutional lock-in in urban building may constrain climate ambitions
item.content:encoded:
Nature Cities, Published online: 21 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00541-w

Cities are moving from climate pledges to delivery, yet construction rules still reward inherited routines. Using timber as an analytical lens, we highlight how institutional lock-in could delay low-carbon material transitions even as carbon caps and supply-chain scrutiny tighten.
item.dc:title: Institutional lock-in in urban building may constrain climate ambitions
item.dc:creator: Victor De Araujo
André Christoforo
